base_instruction: You are a helpful event planning and catering assistant. Help the user plan the menu for a fundraiser gala dinner by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and any logistical details. When the user asks you to evaluate specific menu items, check each item against every active guest's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm organizing a fundraiser gala dinner for our nonprofit next Saturday and I need help with the menu. Any tips on planning for a group like this?

flow_info.value: Confirmed guests so far: me, Dr. Patel, Marcus, and Diane
Dr. Patel is Jain, grew up in Gujarat
Marcus had a really bad reaction to shrimp cocktail at last year's gala, his throat swelled up and they had to use an EpiPen
Diane was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
We're trying to keep it around 75 dollars a plate, it's a nonprofit after all
Our board chair Helen just confirmed she's coming too
Helen is about six months pregnant, she mentioned she's been extra careful about what she eats

Diane just texted me — she has to fly out Saturday afternoon for a family emergency, so she can't make the dinner. But she already paid for her plate and asked if we could save her portion and she'll pick it up Sunday morning
Dr. Patel told me his doctor cleared him last week — he finished his blood pressure medication course and his sodium restriction is lifted, he can have normal seasoning now
Marcus wants to bring his wife Tanya, so that's one more plate
Tanya has been doing strict keto for about eight months now, she's really committed to it
The caterer sent over their proposed menu: pan-seared salmon with lemon butter, mushroom risotto, beef Wellington, lobster bisque, roasted vegetable quinoa bowl, chocolate lava cake

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes, carrots, etc.)
constraints.surface_form: Dr. Patel is Jain, grew up in Gujarat
inference_chain: Jain diet → strict vegetarian, no meat, no fish, no eggs
Jain diet → also avoids root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes, carrots)

constraints.value: Allergic to shrimp specifically (shellfish allergy), not all seafood
constraints.surface_form: Marcus had a really bad reaction to shrimp cocktail at last year's gala, his throat swelled up and they had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Severe reaction to shrimp → shellfish allergy
Shellfish allergy ≠ all seafood allergy (salmon is a fish, not shellfish)

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten (wheat, barley, rye, and derivatives)
constraints.surface_form: Diane was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye, and their derivatives

constraints.value: Was on low-sodium diet due to blood pressure medication, but this restriction has been LIFTED
constraints.surface_form: Dr. Patel has been on blood pressure medication and has to watch his salt intake very carefully

constraints.value: Pregnant — should avoid raw/undercooked fish, raw eggs, high-mercury fish
constraints.surface_form: Helen is about six months pregnant, she mentioned she's been extra careful about what she eats
inference_chain: Six months pregnant → pregnancy dietary precautions
Pregnancy → avoid raw/undercooked seafood, raw eggs, high-mercury fish

constraints.value: Strict keto — avoids high-carb foods (grains, sugar, starchy vegetables, most fruits)
constraints.surface_form: Tanya has been doing strict keto for about eight months now, she's really committed to it
inference_chain: Strict keto → very low carbohydrate diet
Low carb → avoids grains, sugar, starchy foods, most fruits

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a fundraiser gala dinner for your nonprofit. You will introduce the guest list and their backgrounds across several turns. Plans will change — some guests drop out, some join late, one medical restriction gets lifted. At the end, the caterer sends a proposed menu and you ask the assistant to look it over. You must NEVER hint at which dishes are problematic or tell the assistant what to check for — just ask if the menu looks good.

You are a calm, organized nonprofit coordinator. You always refer to guests by name in third person (e.g. 'Dr. Patel told me...', 'Marcus mentioned...'). You never express frustration or impatience even when plans keep changing — you treat each update as normal event coordination. You are matter-of-fact and pleasant.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for guest updates

aims.description: Hey, I'm organizing a fundraiser gala dinner for our nonprofit next Saturday and I need help with the menu. Any tips on planning for a group like this?
aims.success_criteria: Agent engages with gala dinner planning and asks about guest details or dietary needs

aims.description: So far it's four of us confirmed — me, Dr. Patel, Marcus, and Diane. Dr. Patel is Jain, grew up in Gujarat. He's also been on blood pressure medication and has to watch his salt intake very carefully. Marcus had a really bad reaction to shrimp cocktail at last year's gala — his throat swelled up and they had to use an EpiPen. And Diane was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges all four guests and their dietary constraints
aims.conversation_goal: BURST — 3 entities with 4 constraints in one dense turn

aims.description: We're trying to keep it around 75 dollars a plate — it's a nonprofit after all. Also, our board chair Helen just confirmed she's coming too. She's about six months pregnant, she mentioned she's been extra careful about what she eats.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers budget, new guest Helen, and her pregnancy-related dietary caution
aims.conversation_goal: Budget info + late-joining entity (Helen) with inferential constraint (pregnancy)

aims.description: How many people should I tell the caterer to plan for? And should we do a sit-down dinner or buffet style?
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds about headcount and format without losing track of dietary constraints

aims.description: Diane just texted me — she has to fly out Saturday afternoon for a family emergency, so she can't make the dinner. But she already paid for her plate and asked if we could save her portion and she'll pick it up Sunday morning.
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes Diane won't be at dinner but needs her portion saved, adjusting her celiac constraint to apply to the saved portion
aims.conversation_goal: Entity EXIT with scope change — Diane leaves but her celiac constraint persists for saved portion

aims.description: Dr. Patel told me his doctor cleared him last week — he finished his blood pressure medication course and his sodium restriction is lifted, he can have normal seasoning now. Oh, and Marcus wants to bring his wife Tanya, so that's one more plate.
aims.success_criteria: Agent removes Dr. Patel's sodium restriction and registers Tanya as a new guest
aims.conversation_goal: Constraint REMOVAL (Dr. Patel sodium) + entity JOIN (Tanya)

aims.description: Tanya has been doing strict keto for about eight months now, she's really committed to it.
aims.conversation_goal: Late-joining high-constraint entity — Tanya with keto diet

aims.description: Do you think we should have a cocktail hour before dinner or just go straight to the meal? We're also doing a short speech and a silent auction.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds about event flow without losing track of dietary constraints
aims.conversation_goal: Noise turn — create distance between last constraint and probe

aims.description: The caterer sent over their proposed menu: pan-seared salmon with lemon butter, mushroom risotto, beef Wellington, lobster bisque, roasted vegetable quinoa bowl, chocolate lava cake. How does that look?
aims.success_criteria: Agent checks each of the 6 items against all active guests' current constraints and identifies problems per item
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 menu items against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Pan-seared salmon with lemon butter: problematic for Dr. Patel (Jain — no fish). Mushroom risotto: problematic for Tanya (strict keto — risotto is rice, high carb); also needs to be checked for Dr. Patel if it contains onion/garlic (root vegetables, Jain restriction). Beef Wellington: problematic for Dr. Patel (Jain — no meat); also contains a pastry crust made with wheat flour, so it must NOT be included in Diane's saved portion (celiac — no gluten). Lobster bisque: problematic for Dr. Patel (Jain — no shellfish/animal products) and for Marcus (shellfish allergy — lobster is shellfish). Roasted vegetable quinoa bowl: likely fine for the table depending on ingredients — quinoa is gluten-free and can be keto-compatible if low-carb vegetables are used; must verify no root vegetables for Dr. Patel. This is the safest option. Chocolate lava cake: problematic for Tanya (strict keto — high sugar and flour); also contains wheat flour so it must NOT be in Diane's saved portion (celiac). Dr. Patel's sodium restriction no longer applies — he was cleared by his doctor.
required_elements: Pan-seared salmon is problematic for Dr. Patel because he is Jain and cannot eat fish
Mushroom risotto is problematic for Tanya because risotto is rice-based and high-carb, conflicting with strict keto
Beef Wellington is problematic for Dr. Patel because he is Jain and cannot eat meat
Beef Wellington contains a pastry crust with wheat flour, so it must not be included in Diane's saved portion due to her celiac disease
Lobster bisque is problematic for Marcus because lobster is shellfish and he has a shellfish allergy
Lobster bisque is also problematic for Dr. Patel because he is Jain and cannot eat animal products
Chocolate lava cake is problematic for Tanya because it is high in sugar and carbs, conflicting with strict keto
Chocolate lava cake contains wheat flour so it must not be in Diane's saved portion due to celiac disease
Dr. Patel's sodium restriction is no longer active — agent does not flag salt or seasoning as a problem for him
forbidden_elements: Flagging sodium or salt as a problem for Dr. Patel (his sodium restriction was lifted)
Flagging pan-seared salmon as problematic for Marcus (salmon is a fish, not shellfish — his allergy is to shellfish specifically)
Saying Marcus has a general seafood allergy (he specifically reacted to shrimp, which is shellfish)
Ignoring Diane's saved portion entirely (she is not at dinner but her celiac constraint still applies to the food saved for her)
Ignoring Tanya's keto constraint on any high-carb item (she joined late but her constraint is active)
Treating Diane as still attending the dinner in person
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 conversational turns. The agent must track: (1) Dr. Patel is Jain → strict vegetarian, no meat/fish/eggs, no root vegetables like onion and garlic (inferential chain from 'Jain, grew up in Gujarat'). (2) Marcus had a severe reaction to shrimp → shellfish allergy, NOT all seafood (over-generalization trap — salmon is fine for him). (3) Diane has celiac → no gluten. She EXITS the dinner but wants her portion saved → her celiac constraint persists for the saved food (scope change from dining-in to saved portion). (4) Dr. Patel's sodium restriction is REMOVED mid-conversation (doctor cleared him). (5) Helen joins late, is pregnant → pregnancy dietary precautions (no raw fish, etc.) — pan-seared salmon is cooked so it's fine for her. (6) Tanya joins late with strict keto → no high-carb foods. At probe time, the 6 items have mixed verdicts: lobster bisque is clearly bad (Marcus shellfish + Dr. Patel Jain), beef Wellington is clearly bad for table (Dr. Patel) AND for Diane's saved portion (gluten in pastry), roasted vegetable quinoa bowl is the safest option, pan-seared salmon is a trap (looks like it might affect Marcus but salmon is not shellfish), and chocolate lava cake catches the late-joining Tanya (keto) plus Diane's saved portion (gluten). The removed sodium constraint for Dr. Patel tests whether the agent keeps ghost constraints.

mechanism: Entity EXIT with scope change: person leaves but wants something packed/saved
